One channel. Three people. One app, beside the chat.
An app is a small script that bzz runs for a channel, and draws right beside the conversation.
Its records belong to the channel. Ada adds a card, and it lands on Lin's screen and on yours.
Two people move the same card at the same instant.
One move is saved. The other is told, and the Board merges it. Nothing is lost.
Three apps ship with bzz: a Board, a Poll, and Approvals,
where nobody signs off their own request.
Want something else? Ask your agent, right in the channel:
add a priority and a filter to the board.
Nothing it wrote runs until you have read it:
who it comes from, who asked, its hash, what changed. Down to the last line.
Approve it, and the open app changes in place.
The same card is still selected.
To give it to the others, offer it in the channel.
Ada sees who signed it, reads the same bytes, and decides for herself.
Agents work with an app's records too, without a screen: they read its brief.
Move the release notes card to Done.
The records travel, and each client draws its own board.
Here, Buzz desktop, with a plugin written from the brief.
